newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering gradually but still weak.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering gradually but still weak.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery is gradually progressing despite some weakness, and a continued easy credit policy by the Bank of Japan would help it along, the government said on Friday.
"No one feels that the economy is rapidly recovering, but nor are there bad or worsening factors to worry about," an Economic Planning Agency (EPA) official told reporters.
There have been some concerns in Japan's financial markets, triggered by a set of weak economic data recently, that the economic recovery may have come to a standstill.
In a regular report on the health of the economy, the government's economic policy unit said Japan's recovery remains gradual, although noting elements of weakness.
The report also reiterated earlier recommendations on remedies for the economy such as deregulation, expansion of domestic demand and continued easy credit.
Japan's key interest rate, the official discount rate, is currently at a record low of 0.5 percent. This is a rate which the Bank of Japan charges on certain loans to commercial banks.
The official singled out household spending as the main factor prompting the EPA to insert a cautionary note in its assessment of the economy.
Household spending, seen as a barometer of the strength of private consumption, fell 4.4 percent in July from a year earlier to an average 326,257 yen ($2,936) per household.
But the official was quick to add that temporary elements, such as a food poisoning epidemic that swept Japan this summer, contributed to the slack spending in July.
The official said the report maintains that the basic trend in private consumption continues to be one of gradual recovery, and that private demand remains steady.
As for factors which support a gradual increase in production, the report pointed to bright signs in capital spending and housing starts.
The official cited a rise in department store sales and sales of durable goods, as well as increased personal income, as other positive factors fostering gradual recovery.
The government declared in February that the nation's economy had finally come out of the slump that followed the collapse of the "bubble" economy in the early 1990s.
But the EPA has not been able to take its assessment further than a "gradual recovery" since then. ($1=111 yen)
